The ammonium ion is a very weak acid. Its conjugate base ammonia is a moder- ately weak base.

When two bases compete for protons, the stronger base dominates the equilib- rium state in the sense that it holds the larger fraction of protons and is therefore present in a lesser amount in its basic form at equilibrium. The stronger acid do- nates hydrogen ions to the stronger base, producing a weaker acid and a weaker base at equilibrium. To see this consider the equilibrium
